Consult Summary:
- 40-year-old patient with 3 weeks of left-sided decreased hearing and left facial numbness, with intermittent left-sided tinnitus and occasional dizziness; clinician’s preliminary impression is possible Bell’s palsy; plan for same-day in-person neurological and otoscopic examination.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Left-sided reduced hearing and left facial numbness.
- Timeline:
  - Onset: ~3 weeks ago.
  - Course: Persistent; numbness present most of the time and currently present during consult.
- Location/character:
  - Numbness: Left side of face around the left ear and along the left jawline.
  - Hearing: Left ear decreased hearing.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Intermittent ringing (tinnitus) in the left ear.
  - Occasional dizziness associated with the ringing.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No limb weakness or numbness elsewhere.
  - No dysphagia, no speech difficulties.
  - No visual problems.
  - No ear discharge, no ear pain.
  - No fever.
  - Denies using cotton buds.
- Impact on function: Reduced training at work due to symptoms.
- Patient concerns: Anxiety about seriousness; seeking reassurance.

Past Medical History:
- Nasal polyps; uses nasal spray as needed (medication name not recalled).
- History of “labyrinthitis” in the past; no ongoing issues reported.
- No other chronic illnesses disclosed.

Medications:
- Nasal spray for nasal polyps, as needed; name and dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Rennies (OTC antacid), as needed; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- No other regular medications reported.

Allergies:
- Latex.

Social History:
- Occupation: Jockey; training reduced due to symptoms.
- Living situation: Initially stated living alone, then stated living with partner (conflict noted).
- Pets: None reported.
- Tobacco, alcohol, substance use: Not documented.

Family History:
- Brother with neurofibromatosis.
- Otherwise noncontributory per patient.

Physical Examination:
- Not performed during video consult; no vitals documented.

Investigations:
- None during this encounter.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Left-sided decreased hearing with left facial numbness; intermittent tinnitus and occasional dizziness.
  - Assessment: Preliminary clinical impression of possible Bell’s palsy per clinician; needs confirmation with physical examination and neurological assessment; otoscopic exam to evaluate ear.
  - Plan:
    - Same-day, face-to-face appointment in clinic for full neurological examination and otoscopic assessment.
    - Administrative team to book urgent appointment; patient to call support team number after 5 minutes to arrange a convenient central London clinic slot.
    - Reassurance provided that this does not appear life-threatening based on history; definitive assessment pending in-person exam.
- Issue 2: Patient anxiety regarding condition.
  - Plan:
    - Reassurance provided; advised urgent in-person evaluation today for definitive assessment.

- Issue 3: Nasal polyps (intermittent).
  - Plan:
    - Continue nasal spray as needed (no changes discussed).

General plan items:
- Ensure appointment is attended today as advised.

  - Vitals not obtained.
  - No in-person physical examination documented in this encounter.
  - Full medication reconciliation incomplete (nasal spray name, dosing not documented; OTC use details not fully documented).
  - Past surgical history, immunizations, gynecologic/obstetric history (if applicable), and detailed ROS not documented.
  - Tobacco, alcohol, and other substance use not documented.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Living situation: Patient stated living alone, then stated living with partner (conflict noted).

  - Minor pauses/inaudible fragments; overall adequate to extract key clinical details.
